written.myAnswer: Data visualization presents information visually, making complex data easier to understand. It helps people quickly identify patterns, trends, and relationships.
A line graph is used to show how data changes over time. For example, it can show a student's height at different ages.
A scatter plot displays paired values for two variables and can help reveal a relationship between them. For example, it could show students' study hours and test scores.

Data visualization presents data in visual forms such as charts and graphs, helping reveal patterns and trends. For example, a bar chart can compare sales of different products, a pie chart can show how a budget is divided, a line graph can show temperature changes over time, and a scatter plot can show the relationship between advertising spending and sales.

Visualizations make data easier to understand and help decision-makers quickly spot patterns, trends, and comparisons. Businesses can use charts, graphs, and dashboards to make informed decisions, such as identifying which products sell best.

Nominal data consists of unordered categories, such as product types, which can be displayed in a bar chart. Ordinal data consists of ordered categories without equal intervals, such as satisfaction ratings, which can be displayed in a bar chart. Discrete data consists of separate countable values, such as the number of books students read, which can be shown in a dot plot. Continuous data can take any value within a range, such as daily temperatures, and can be shown in a line graph.
